summary: Layer assignment from the E¹₂g–A₁g separation (Lee et al. 2010), cross-checked against the Si 520 cm⁻¹ attenuation: B ≈ 1L (separation 19.2 cm⁻¹); A ≈ 2L (21.5 cm⁻¹); D ≈ few-layer, roughly 4–6L and not distinguishable from thicker (24.3 cm⁻¹); C is bulk-like (25.1 cm⁻¹, ≳10 layers and probably much thicker). Thickness ordering is B < A < D < C. The separation saturates above about 4–5 layers, so D and C cannot be given an exact layer number from these spectra. All four are 2H-MoS2 with sharp, well-resolved modes and no sign of disorder. There is a cosmic-ray spike in C at 265.1 cm⁻¹ that is not a Raman mode. AFM, low-frequency Raman or PL is needed to fix the layer numbers.

observations.evidence: Pseudo-Voigt fits give E¹₂g = 383.90±0.02 and A₁g = 403.09±0.12 cm⁻¹, so Δ = 19.2 cm⁻¹. This is the smallest separation of the set and is in the monolayer range (~18–20 cm⁻¹). E¹₂g area is 2.0e3, about half of flake A. The Si 520 cm⁻¹ line is only weakly attenuated: Si/E¹₂g height ratio is 2.5, the highest of the four.
observations.source: Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), Fig. 2 (peak positions and separation vs. layer number)

observations.evidence: E¹₂g = 383.36±0.01 and A₁g = 404.85±0.08 cm⁻¹, so Δ = 21.5 cm⁻¹, in the 2L range (~21–22 cm⁻¹). The E¹₂g area is 4.2e3, about 2.1× that of B, as expected for 2L vs 1L. The Si/E¹₂g ratio is 1.04. A₁g is broad (FWHM 6.6 cm⁻¹ vs 2.1 for E¹₂g) and the I(A₁g)/I(E¹₂g) height ratio is 0.33.
observations.source: Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), Fig. 2

observations.finding: Flake D is few-layer (about 4–6L), with 'thicker than 4L' as the firm statement. Its thickness is less than that of C.
observations.evidence: E¹₂g = 382.37±0.01 and A₁g = 406.63±0.03 cm⁻¹, so Δ = 24.3 cm⁻¹. This is just below the bulk value (~25) and above 3L (~23). The Si 520 line is still clearly visible (Si/E¹₂g = 0.37) and the E¹₂g area is the largest of the set (8.4e3), so the flake is not extremely thick. A₁g FWHM is 4.6 cm⁻¹, broader than in C.
observations.source: Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), Fig. 2; Li et al., Adv. Funct. Mater. 22, 1385 (2012) for saturation of the separation above ~4L

observations.evidence: E¹₂g = 382.24±0.04 and A₁g = 407.31±0.07 cm⁻¹, so Δ = 25.1 cm⁻¹, the bulk value. A₁g FWHM is 3.1 cm⁻¹ (the narrowest of the set, near the resolution limit) and E¹₂g FWHM is 2.2. The Si line is strongly suppressed (Si/E¹₂g = 0.21, Si peak height only ~69 counts above a ~350 baseline). The ordering of Si suppression (A, B > D > C) matches the separation ordering.
observations.source: Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), Fig. 2

observations.finding: The trend with thickness is E¹₂g softening and A₁g stiffening: E¹₂g goes 383.9 → 383.4 → 382.4 → 382.2 and A₁g goes 403.1 → 404.9 → 406.6 → 407.3 cm⁻¹ for B → A → D → C.
observations.evidence: This is the usual monolayer-to-bulk evolution, attributed to interlayer coupling and a stiffer out-of-plane restoring force. E¹₂g changes by only ~1.7 cm⁻¹ against ~4.2 cm⁻¹ for A₁g, so the separation is the better thickness indicator. The E¹₂g shift is comparable to the effect of small strain.
observations.source: Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), Fig. 2

observations.finding: Crystal quality is good in all flakes, with no evidence of defects, a phase change, or a layer-dependent E¹₂g splitting.
observations.evidence: E¹₂g FWHM is 2.0–2.2 cm⁻¹ for all four flakes. This is at or below the stated ~2.7 cm⁻¹ resolution, so it is resolution-limited. The Si line sits at 519.99–520.04 cm⁻¹ in A, B and D, which also confirms the calibration (C's Si fit is too weak to use). There is no extra peak near 150–340 cm⁻¹ (J₁/J₂/J₃, which would indicate 1T/1T′) apart from the C spike. Two-component A₁g fits are not supported statistically (BIC does not improve for A, B or D).
observations.source: Phase markers: Eda et al., Nano Lett. 11, 5111 (2011); Yang et al., Phys. Rev. B 95, 2017 (J modes of 1T′ MoS2)

observations.finding: The sharp line at 265.1 cm⁻¹ in spectrum C is a cosmic-ray spike, not a Raman mode.
observations.evidence: It is a single pixel (3317 counts vs ~350 baseline; neighbouring pixels at 349 and 355). Real modes here are at least 2–3 points wide at this ~0.55 cm⁻¹ step. I excluded it from the fits.

observations.finding: The wider A₁g in the thin and few-layer flakes (6.6, 5.4 and 4.6 cm⁻¹ for A, B and D vs 3.1 for C) is unexplained and is not due to a resolvable second peak.
observations.evidence: A₁g FWHM is 2–3× the E¹₂g FWHM in A, B and D. Two-Lorentzian fits did not improve BIC. The broadening may come from doping or charge inhomogeneity, laser heating, or a local-thickness mix within the laser spot (40× spot ~1 µm).
observations.source: Chakraborty et al., Phys. Rev. B 85, 161403 (2012) (A₁g softening and broadening with electron doping)

caveats: The E¹₂g–A₁g separation saturates above about 4–5 layers, so D and C cannot be given a layer number from these spectra. Si 520 attenuation is a relative thickness indicator for D vs C only; it depends on the 285 nm SiO2 interference, absorption at 514.5 nm and focus.

Strain mainly shifts E¹₂g (biaxial strain moves it by several cm⁻¹ per %) and doping or charge transfer mainly shifts A₁g. Either could mimic a one-layer error in the separation. B vs A differs by 2.3 cm⁻¹, which is larger than the fit error but not unambiguous on its own. Substrate-induced strain or charge transfer in 1L and 2L flakes is plausible.

Absolute intensities are not comparable between spectra. Integration time, power, focus and the SiO2 interference all differ (C has weak MoS2 signal overall, D a strong one). Only within-spectrum ratios (Si/MoS2, A₁g/E¹₂g) are meaningful. The A₁g/E¹₂g ratio (0.33–0.70) varies without a clean thickness trend, so I did not use it.
Fit errors are statistical only. With ~0.55–0.6 cm⁻¹ point spacing and ~2.7 cm⁻¹ resolution, a ±0.2–0.3 cm⁻¹ systematic shift is plausible. The Si line at 520.0 cm⁻¹ suggests the calibration is good.

Laser heating at 514.5 nm in air can soften and broaden the modes of thin flakes on SiO2. I did not check power dependence. The baseline in A and D rises with shift (a sloping background, possibly weak PL or the SiO2/Si background). PL is expected from 1L and weak from 2L at 514.5 nm, but the PL range was not recorded.

The spectra start at 150 cm⁻¹, so the low-frequency interlayer shear and breathing modes (~20–40 cm⁻¹), which give the cleanest layer count up to ~10 layers, are not covered. The 2LA(M) region near 450 cm⁻¹ is too weak and noisy to use.
questions_for_user: What laser power at the sample, integration time and grating were used for each flake? This tells me whether the A₁g broadening is heating, and whether the intensities can be compared.
Were the spectra taken at a single spot per flake? Flakes with terraces can mix thicknesses within the ~1 µm spot, which would broaden A₁g.
Do you have PL spectra (the 1L A exciton at ~1.85 eV) or optical contrast values for these flakes? Either would confirm B = 1L and A = 2L independently.
Can you record the low-frequency range (below 100 cm⁻¹, shear and breathing modes) or take an AFM scan? That would fix the layer numbers of D and C, which the high-frequency modes cannot do.
Does the cosmic-ray spike in C appear in a repeat acquisition? Repeating the measurement would confirm it is an artifact.

limits: Layer numbers for D and C are lower bounds (D ≳ 4L, C bulk-like) and come from the high-frequency modes alone.
The 1L vs 2L assignments for B and A rest on the position of a single separation value and the relative E¹₂g intensity. Strain or doping could shift them by about one layer.

The data say nothing about stacking order, because stacking-sensitive interlayer modes are outside the measured range (≥150 cm⁻¹). It says nothing about lateral thickness uniformity or the flakes' optical appearance.
The spectra do not distinguish strain from doping, and they do not give the flake temperature.
